summary: Plan a standalone, offline Godot 4.x GDScript Android arcade game provisionally titled Market Rickshaw Rush. Proposed GitHub repository: yogeshaneja/market-rickshaw-rush-godot (availability check and human approval required; do not create). This is separate from Market Stall Challenge. Adults steer an original auto-rickshaw between three lanes on a colourful fictional Indian market route, avoiding crates, potholes, carts and parked vehicles while collecting delivery tokens. MVP: one looping route, three difficulties, capped speed progression, seeded fair spawning, distance/token scoring, tutorial, pause/retry, bilingual English/Hindi UI, local best scores and reduce-effects setting. Seven UI screens, original 2D art, silent prototype, no pedestrians or animals in collision gameplay. Use Godot Compatibility renderer initially for budget Android support, subject to installed-version and device verification. Fixed-step physics and deterministic spawn rules must remain independent of decorative animation. All gameplay and assets bundled offline; no backend, accounts, cloud, AI calls, ads, payments, analytics, Expo or third-party plugins. Prepare release drafts without signing or publishing. Estimated 20 developer working days for MVP and release preparation, excluding unpredictable tooling setup, external approvals and store review. Human approvals remain mandatory for repository creation, implementation, native export, asset rights, gameplay balance, signing, developer-account setup, hosting, merge and publication. All functionality and checks described are planned, not implemented or executed.
acceptanceCriteria: A verified stable Godot 4.x installation runs the GDScript project using the Compatibility renderer. Record exact editor version, project structure, renderer, export templates and Android toolchain versions before implementation. No version or tool availability is assumed.

Home, Tutorial, Game, Pause, Results, Settings and About/Credits screens work with consistent original market-themed visuals. English is default; every visible menu, instruction, result, setting and error has equivalent Hindi text.

The player automatically advances through one continuously scrolling fictional market route. Exactly three valid lanes exist. Swipe left/right, optional visible touch buttons and desktop keyboard inputs move one lane per accepted command; edge inputs never move outside the road.

Use InputMap actions move_left, move_right, pause and confirm with desktop key mappings and touch input adapters. Gestures have minimum-distance and direction thresholds; taps on UI controls cannot accidentally trigger swipes.

Three difficulty presets define documented initial speed, capped acceleration, obstacle density and scoring rules. Movement uses fixed physics ticks and delta-based distances; outcomes remain consistent under varied rendering frame rates.

Seeded obstacle generation supports reproducible sequences. Every generated section has a reachable safe lane path based on player lane-change time, spawn spacing, obstacle dimensions and speed. No unavoidable three-lane barriers, overlapping hazards or unfair immediate follow-up hazards occur.

Crates, potholes, delivery carts and parked vehicles have explicit collision shapes. Only gameplay collision logic determines damage. One valid collision ends the run once; decorative effects and overlapping collision signals cannot create repeated penalties.

Delivery tokens are visually distinct from hazards and award a fixed configurable bonus once per collection. Distance scoring increases monotonically while actively running. Pausing, countdowns, game-over animations and restarting cannot inflate scores.

Pause, resume, restart and game-over transitions are valid and idempotent. Focus loss or Android backgrounding immediately suspends simulation and input; returning requires an explicit resume action and visible countdown before movement restarts.
A short tutorial explains lane changes, obstacles, tokens and pause. Results display distance, tokens, final score, difficulty and best score, with immediate retry and return-home actions.

Language, reduce-effects preference and per-difficulty best scores persist under user://. Invalid, missing or corrupted files recover to safe defaults. A confirmed score reset removes scores only and preserves language and effects settings.

Reduce-effects disables particles, camera shake, nonessential bobbing and celebration motion. Static feedback preserves hazard visibility, collision state, collection confirmation and readable results. No flashing effects are required.

Original saffron, coral, turquoise, mango-yellow, leaf-green and deep-blue artwork uses Godot 2D drawing or verified reusable bundled sprites. All assets have provenance/license records; labels remain separate localized text, never baked into illustrations.

Devanagari shaping, font coverage, readable contrast, scalable text, touch-target sizes and narrow-screen layouts are reviewed on real Android hardware. Obstacles and tokens remain distinguishable by shape without relying on colour alone.

A localized home reminder says future app updates may introduce new routes or content without promising availability. Check on Google Play remains hidden until package ID and published listing are verified; a user tap opens the app's own listing with HTTPS fallback and graceful failure.

Headless deterministic tests cover lane boundaries, spawn reproducibility, safe-path reachability, scoring, duplicate collision prevention and persistence validation. Desktop interactive tests separately cover visuals, input, transitions, localization and effects.

Real budget Android phones are used to record observed frame pacing, memory, startup, heat, touch responsiveness, background/resume and offline behaviour. Performance is measured rather than assumed; no fixed FPS guarantee is claimed.

Android deployment requires verified export templates, SDK, JDK, package ID and approved export configuration. Test direct USB ADB and paired wireless ADB where supported. Confirm standalone installation, launch and offline play without Expo Go.

Four app-specific release drafts exist: bilingual store copy with asset/screenshot briefs, privacy policy, signed-AAB instructions and device/content declaration worksheets. Unknown developer identity, contact, account and hosting details remain explicitly unset.

No repository, branch, build, signing key, AAB, upload, publication or approval is created or claimed by this planning response. Developer and human reviewers explicitly approve subsequent implementation and release gates.
implementationSteps: 1. Verify actual Godot stable 4.x version, repository contents, existing assets, scripts, licenses and export tooling. Confirm proposed repository-name availability. Record engine and platform assumptions. Obtain human approval before repository creation or implementation.

2. Define scene architecture: Main, Home, Tutorial, Game, Pause, Results, Settings and Credits. Within Game use Road, SceneryLayers, Player, SpawnManager, Obstacles, Tokens, CollisionManager, HUD and Effects nodes. Keep simulation, rendering and UI separate.

3. Design GDScript modules for GameState, RunController, DifficultyConfig, SpawnPlanner, CollisionRules, ScoreCalculator, InputController, SaveService and LocalizationService. Specify clear signals, lifecycle transitions and dependency boundaries.

4. Establish InputMap actions for left, right, pause and confirm. Plan swipe detection, touch buttons and desktop keyboard mapping. Resolve gesture conflicts with Control nodes, define swipe thresholds and test edge-lane behaviour.

5. Specify a fixed physics timestep and world-distance model. Use _physics_process(delta) for authoritative movement and collision decisions. Keep logical lane indices separate from visual interpolation. Set documented speed caps and progression curves for three difficulties.

6. Design seeded spawn planning with independent deterministic random streams for hazards and optional decoration. Generate ahead in distance-based segments. Use reachability checks accounting for lane-change cooldown, player dimensions, speed, reaction margin and obstacle clearance; reject and regenerate unsafe layouts.

7. Define collision layers, masks and shapes for rickshaw, obstacles and delivery tokens. Use Area2D or appropriate 2D physics nodes, with single-hit guards and authoritative run-state checks. Avoid rigid-body vehicle simulation and pedestrian/animal collisions.

8. Define scoring: distance accumulated only in active play, fixed token bonuses, per-difficulty final scores and best-score comparisons. Specify integer or consistently rounded score calculations and deterministic reset behaviour.

9. Create original 2D visual specifications for rickshaw, stalls, awnings, road, fruit crates, carts, buildings and bunting. Use geometry or approved reusable sprites. Record source, creator, license, modifications and attribution requirements. Prototype remains silent.

10. Plan layered scrolling scenery, road markings, visual lane interpolation, subtle wheel/body motion, collection feedback and short results celebration. Use Godot Tween, AnimationPlayer and bounded particles. Ensure effect completion never controls gameplay outcomes.

11. Implement screen flow specifications for Home, Tutorial, Game, Pause, Results, Settings and Credits. Define explicit pause, restart, return-home, game-over and background/resume transitions. Use a visible resume countdown with gameplay simulation stopped.

12. Define localization resources for English and Hindi, including tutorial, results, settings, errors and future-content reminder. Bundle a verified Devanagari-capable font with appropriate rights. Validate shaping, line wrapping, scalable UI and narrow Android layouts.

13. Specify local persistence using versioned ConfigFile or JSON in user://, with schema validation, bounded values, temporary-file writes and recovery defaults. Save preferences and best scores. Add confirmed score reset preserving language and reduce-effects preferences.

14. Plan reduce-effects behaviour and static equivalents. Disable camera shake, particles, decorative bouncing and animated celebrations when enabled. Retain clear colour-and-shape hazard cues, collision feedback and visible collection/score information.

15. Define automated GDScript/headless tests using deterministic simulation helpers. Cover spawn safety, seeded replay, collision idempotency, lane bounds, scoring, pause transitions and corrupted saves. Distinguish headless checks from actual rendered and device tests.

16. Prepare desktop playtesting matrix covering keyboard, mouse/touch emulation, varied render rates, difficulty balancing, spawn fairness, tutorial comprehension, visual clarity and restart. Record findings and require human review of balance, Hindi text and asset rights.

17. Prepare Android export prerequisites: verify installed export templates, Android SDK/build-tools/platform-tools, compatible JDK, package ID and device settings. After approval, test USB debugging or wireless ADB pairing, direct installation and offline play on budget phones.

18. Draft release step 1: English store title Market Rickshaw Rush; short description Dodge market obstacles and deliver tokens in a colourful offline rickshaw runner. Hindi title बाज़ार रिक्शा रश; short description रंगीन ऑफ़लाइन रिक्शा गेम में बाधाओं से बचें और डिलीवरी टोकन जुटाएँ। Long descriptions explain three lanes, three difficulties, offline play and no accounts. Screenshot briefs: home, gameplay, hazards, results, Hindi UI and settings; original icon/feature graphic only.

19. Draft release steps 2–3: Privacy policy states intended offline-only operation, local scores/preferences, no account, ads, analytics or developer-operated data collection; verify actual SDK/network behaviour before publication. Secure AAB guide covers approved package ID, private upload key, protected keystore/passwords, backup, release export, signature verification and Play App Signing; no signing performed.

20. Draft release step 4: device/content worksheets cover tested models/Android versions, performance evidence, offline operation, accessibility, target audience, content rating, Data safety, permissions, asset licenses and declarations. Mark developer name, email, public policy URL, hosting, account, package ID and publication status UNSET. Gate store-check button on verified live listing. Require separate approvals for account setup, hosting, signing, upload and publication.
risks: Godot version, actual repository files, available export templates and SDK/JDK installations are unknown. Validate before coding; renderer compatibility and export configuration may require adjustment.

Safe-path guarantees depend on measured lane-change timing, collision shapes, speed caps and reaction margins. Seeded reachability tests plus human gameplay review are mandatory; random selection alone is insufficient.

Compatibility renderer is the initial low-end Android choice, not a universal performance guarantee. Measure frame pacing, memory and heat on actual budget devices; reduce particles, draw calls and texture sizes if needed.
Hindi translations, Devanagari shaping, bundled font licensing and small-screen readability require verification by a competent Hindi reviewer and real-device testing.
Original artwork and any externally sourced reusable assets need documented rights and attribution. Do not assume Godot supplies finished vehicle sprites or reuse NeonCity intellectual property.

Android package ID, public developer identity, support contact, privacy-policy hosting, Play account status and signing-key custody are UNSET. Publication and store-link activation cannot proceed without verification and approval.

Offline privacy statements must match the final exported application, bundled dependencies and Android permissions. Platform or plugin behaviour must be inspected before completing Play Data safety declarations.
Android focus/background callbacks and process suspension can vary by OS and device. Require actual device evidence for safe pause, countdown resume, save recovery and interruption handling.

The 20-day estimate assumes one route, original lightweight art, silent gameplay, no external plugins and available test devices. Custom illustrations, localization review, export issues and balancing iterations may extend delivery.

Google Play update checking must remain user-initiated and hidden before publication. External store access can fail offline or without Play Store; HTTPS fallback must handle errors without claiming an update exists.
